title: Reduced Zariski closure of a monoid is a group subscheme
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $M\subseteq G(k)$ contain the identity and satisfy $ab\in M$ for all $a,b\in M$. Let $H$ be its reduced Zariski closure in $G$: on each affine open it is defined by the radical ideal of functions vanishing on $M$ in that open. Then multiplication, identity and inverse of $G$ restrict to $H$, making $H\hookrightarrow G$ a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. No affineness, smoothness or connectedness of $G$ or $H$ is assumed.

source.place: Section 1(c): Aside 1.55, p.21 (algebraic submonoids are subgroups), with Theorem 1.45 and Corollary 1.47, pp.19--20 (closed point subgroups and reduced subgroup schemes). Applied to the reduced closure using multiplication on dense rational points; compare the closure step in the referenced Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1 proof. No single Stacks tag states this combined assertion.

proof.text: Write $Z=\overline M$ for closure in the underlying space $|G|$. Finite type gives a finite affine open cover $G=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] each such open is Noetherian as a topological space, and [lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian] makes $|G|$ Noetherian. Thus descending chains of closed subsets of $|G|$ stabilize. The identity point belongs to $Z$ since it belongs to $M$.

source.place: Tag 0053, label lemma-finite-union-Noetherian; finite-type affine cover from the definition; affine Noetherianity as in lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components.

proof.text: For $g\in G(k)$ the morphisms $L_g(x)=gx$ and $R_g(x)=xg$ have inverses $L_{g^{-1}}$ and $R_{g^{-1}}$, by the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme]; hence they induce homeomorphisms of $|G|$. For $m\in M$, $R_m(M)\subseteq M$, so $R_m(Z)=\overline{R_m(M)}\subseteq Z$. If $a\in G(k)$ has underlying point in $Z$, it follows that $am\in Z$ for every $m\in M$. Consequently $L_a(M)\subseteq Z$ and $L_a(Z)=\overline{L_a(M)}\subseteq Z$. In particular the rational points in $Z$ are closed under multiplication. These closure identities use homeomorphisms one at a time.

source.place: Section 1(c), Aside 1.55, printed p.22 (PDF p.34), finite-monoid translation analogy; agent proof using Noetherianity rather than Ax-Grothendieck. Final realization: Theorem 1.45, printed p.19.

proof.text: Fix $a\in G(k)$ lying in $Z$. The subsets $Z\supseteq L_a(Z)\supseteq L_a^2(Z)\supseteq\cdots$ are closed in $|G|$, since $L_a$ is a homeomorphism, and the inclusions follow by repeatedly applying $L_a$ to $L_a(Z)\subseteq Z$. Noetherianity established in step 1 (from [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components, lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian]) gives $L_a^n(Z)=L_a^{n+1}(Z)$ for some $n\geq0$. Apply $L_{a^{-n}}$ to this equality to obtain $Z=L_a(Z)$. As $1\in Z$, there is $z\in Z$ with $az=1$, and the inverse homeomorphism forces this point to be $a^{-1}$. Therefore $S=G(k)\cap Z$ contains the identity and is closed under multiplication and inversion. It is closed in $G(k)$ with its subspace topology.

source.place: Section 1(c), Aside 1.55, printed p.22 (PDF p.34), finite-monoid translation analogy; agent proof using Noetherianity rather than Ax-Grothendieck. Final realization: Theorem 1.45, printed p.19.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-closed-rational-subgroup-realization] to the closed subgroup $S$ just obtained. Its reduced closure $K\hookrightarrow G$ has multiplication, identity and inverse restricted from $G$. The inclusions $M\subseteq S\subseteq Z$ give $\overline S=Z$. To identify $K$ with the $H$ in the statement, on any affine open $U$ the subset $M\cap U$ is dense in $Z\cap U$: every open neighbourhood in $U$ of a point of $Z\cap U$ is also open in $G$ and meets $M$. The zero locus of any section on $U$ is closed in $U$, so a section vanishes on $M\cap U$ exactly when it vanishes on $Z\cap U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] these are precisely the radical ideals defining the reduced induced closed scheme on $Z$. Thus both $H$ and $K$ are that same closed subscheme, and the restricted operations on $K$ supply all the required operations on $H$.

split_report.summary: Retained the statement; proved multiplicative closure by successive translation homeomorphisms and inverse stability by the Noetherian descending chain of translates. Isolated only the independent closed-rational-subgroup realization theorem (Milne 1.45) as a statement-only node. Reused affine Noetherianity, finite-union Noetherianity and the unique reduced induced closed structure. No affineness, smoothness, connectedness, commutativity or characteristic assumption was added.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-42ad70159 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-sfb-closed-rational-subgroup-realization, every cited statement, and Milne iAG2017 §1(c) at the cited places: Theorem 1.45 is on printed p.19 (PDF p.31) and Aside 1.55 on printed p.22 (PDF p.34). The new node is exactly the existence half of Milne 1.45, with the same hypotheses: any field, a finite-type group scheme, a closed subgroup S of G(k), H = (closure of S)_red, the operations restrict, and H(k) = S. It is strictly smaller than the item because it assumes inverse stability, which steps 1–3 prove. Its edge cases hold: S={1} over an imperfect field gives Spec k, and nondense rational points are fine. B1–B7 are satisfied. Step 1: a finite affine cover plus the Mathlib leaves lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components and lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian make |G| Noetherian. Step 2 (elementary): left and right translations are homeomorphisms by the group diagrams and are applied one at a time, giving R_m(Z) ⊆ Z and then L_a(Z) ⊆ Z, with no joint continuity used. Step 3: the descending chain of translates L_a^n(Z) stabilizes; cancelling with L_{a^-n} gives Z = L_a(Z), and bijectivity forces a^-1 into Z, so S = G(k)∩Z is a closed subgroup. Step 4: S has closure Z; M∩U is dense in Z∩U and zero loci are closed, so the item's ideals equal I_Z from lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme (1)–(2), hence H = Z_red = K. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. The duplicate search (rg for 1.45, Zariski closure with subgroup, submonoid, subgroup of G(k)) found only narrower nodes: lem-wf-zariski-closure-subgroup, generic-matrix-locus-subgroup-closure, perfect-field-groupoid-image-closure and semisimple-cyclic-closure. There is no cycle and no SGA source. I accept the tool use of lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme (unit sk-thm-p1). Two cosmetic points: the item's source.place and blueprint.from.place still say Aside 1.55 is on p.21, although the report claims this was corrected (only the step sources were); and the algebraically-closed hypothesis is never used.
